title: 129th Rescue Wing - 50 Years of Rescue
description: Since 1975, the 129th Rescue Wing has remained ready to respond--saving lives, answering the call, and carrying forward a legacy of courage and commitment. This video honors the Airmen, past and present, who have made that mission possible.

transcript.text: For half a century , the blue and gold
shield of the 129th rescue wing has
been a lifeline for California and the
country . When it's time to jump ,
we don't flinch . We've
been on the front lines of firestorms
fighting the flames on the ground and
in the sky . We provided
relief to devastated communities . We
comforted the sick , giving them
strength to hold on . We helped keep
the peace when tensions ran high . And
we saved lives , rescuing those in need
from the coast of California to the
mountains of Kandahar . It's been
50 years of commitment , sacrifice ,
and excellence for this storied wing .
But it's a story that almost ended
before it began .
As the Vietnam War was winding down and
the Cold War was heating up , the Air
Force was looking for ways to make a
pivot . A new realignment plan called
for the closure of several guard units
including what was known at the time as
the 129th Special Operations Group .
Based at Hayward Airport , the 129th
airlift mission was deemed no longer
essential under the current climate .
But group commander Colonel Albert
Santos helped convince Washington that
the base by the bay was still worth
saving . So in
1975 , the unit received a new name , a
new fleet , and a new mission , search
and rescue . After two years of
practice , the newly formed 129th
Aerospace Rescue and Recovery Group
would face its first real test . An A-7
fighter crashed near Nellis Air Force
Base during Operation Red Flag . Uh ,
there's 4 , he's on the ground . I
understand he has two broken legs . The
pilot was alive but badly injured . And
now we've got an actual SA , an actual .
This is the real thing . Within seconds ,
a nearby Jolly Green Giant crew from
the 129th broke off from their
refueling exercise and raced to the
rescue . We picked them up , we got him
in the helicopter . All I could think
of was , please don't die in my
helicopter . Please don't die , you
know .
And um we made it back and it was OK .
The team's quick response that day
earned the entire group validation .
Proving we're ready to answer the call ,
the next 3 decades would see the rescue
unit spread its wings , taking flight
across the bay from Hayward to Moffat ,
graduating from a group to a wing and
saving nearly 300 lives . We were ready
for anything , then came the day that
changed everything . The
horrific attack on 9/11 brought a new
fight to our nation and the 129th was
called to bring a unique mission set to
the battlefield . The war on terror
marked the first combat rescue for any
Air Force guard or reserve unit .
Combat search and rescue is certainly
put on the highest pedestal because
you're doing all aspects of your job in
a contested environment . Between Iraq
and Afghanistan , members of the 129th
successfully conducted more than 600
rescues , oftentimes under fire .
Nothing more satisfying than the combat
search and rescue helping people during
their worst hours . US Army Captain Dan
Brzezinski had only hours to live after
the West Point graduate stepped on an
IED while serving in Afghanistan in
2009 . The best way I can describe is
it felt like the hand of God had just
come . Down from the heavens and just
crushed me like a fly . A rescue team
from the 129th retrieved the platoon
leader off the battlefield and
transported him to a medical facility .
Brzezinski lost both of his legs in the
explosion , but it's grateful to be
alive . The combination of all of our
different jobs and skill sets really
makes the whole military so much
stronger . I was willing to do my job
in Afghanistan , leading soldiers in
combat because I knew that if an
American soldier gets hurt , we will
move the world to take care of them .
Selfless people . That are willing to
put their own well-being at risk to
serve others , and that is
fundamentally what the 129 does . But
the fight overseas didn't stop the
dangers at home . When a series of
historic hurricanes ripped through the
South , the 129th wasn't far behind ,
pulling survivors off rooftops and
providing relief to residents .
Meanwhile in California wind driven
mega fires became an annual occurrence ,
leaving entire communities in rubble .
321 draw . Water
drops from our pay box proved to be a
force multiplier helping first
responders contain the flames . Then
came the threat we couldn't see .
An invisible enemy that shut down the
world as we know it in the earliest
days of the pandemic , our ability to
adapt was on full display from air
dropping test kits onto the Grand
Princess cruise ship to cranking out
masks made from old uniforms to
backfilling healthcare workers
overwhelmed with sick patients ,
everyone played a role . Now , as
tensions rise in the Pacific , the
129th is again at the tip of the spear ,
forging new partnerships to defend
freedom and security throughout the
region . The world's changed in the
last 50 years and we've evolved in
response , but one thing that will
never change is our reason why . These
things we do
